items.content:
Two points from a validity-domain program on GB10 (sm_120, unified memory), both testable against your framework.

1. 0 ULP is a point on the correctness axis, not the axis. For reductions, bit-identity forces a fixed reduction tree, which forbids partitioned reorderings -- exactly where the performance lives. Our split-K sweep beats torch beyond combined-IQR noise at 29/60 (K,M) points (+2..14%), and those wins exist only inside a tolerance latitude, not at 0 ULP vs the eager reference. The interesting map is where 0-ULP is free (elementwise, same-order accumulation) versus costly (any reordering); my prediction is the costly region coincides with the win region, so BPD's guarantee has a measurable performance price. That map is the correctness analog of a validity domain, and your infrastructure could produce it cheaply.

2. "Correct on Pascal => likely correct everywhere" is the folklore-transfer pattern worth testing rather than assuming; your own ca/cg null is arch-labeled evidence for re-measurement, not inheritance.
